title: [recoverability][performance] scenario harness drops: check-j02-lands.sh stops its loop before dropping 004's database, and scenario-db.sh bounds every statement (SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS, default 60), so a drop behind an undrained LISTEN fails instead of holding the test server
prompt:
Spawn, objective 237 [recoverability][performance] (an owner change on rsi/ and scripts/, committed by the lead; no fleet task; the lead's 20:56 contract from the 11-19 ccd hangs; author rev-k; readers rev-i first, rev-b second; R1 answers rev-i's R0 F1/F2 and rev-b's R0 F3, n2): a scenario harness never drops a database WITH (FORCE) while a loop of its own run holds LISTEN, and every harness drop is bounded, so a hang fails instead of holding the test server and suite.lock for every run.

Why. On 2026-11-19 (18:0x and 18:2x) check-j02-lands.sh hung the shared ccd test server twice, about 19 and 13 min.
- Its section [004] dropped its database WITH (FORCE) (in s004_finish, and again in the main part) while section L's `spawn loop` held LISTEN on the run's other database.
- A loop drains that connection only between passes (spawn-postgres wake.rs Listener::wait), so its backend sat blocked sending to it (ClientWrite).
- A backend blocked in a client write never absorbs the server's ProcSignalBarrier, and every DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) waits on it. So the drop waited, every other run's drop queued behind it, and suite.lock stayed held.
- A private-cluster probe (runs/probe-barrier.sh) shows it: a listener that reads nothing, flooded with notifications, waits on ClientWrite; a DROP ... WITH (FORCE) of another database then waits, and statement_timeout '3s' cancels it at 3005 ms with the database left.

Read: rsi/scenarios/check-j02-lands.sh (cleanup, section_004 and s004_finish, section L's loop, the end's "section 004's verdict"), scripts/blackbox/scenario-db.sh (drop, sweep, the logins session).

What changes (owner files only):
- check-j02-lands.sh:
  - s004_finish no longer drops 004's database (a comment says why);
  - the main part, after waiting for section 004, stops section L's loop (kill, wait, loop_pid="") before it drops 004's database;
  - the run's cleanup is unchanged: it stops the loop first, then drops both databases.
- scripts/blackbox/scenario-db.sh:
  - every statement it sends runs under statement_timeout, SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS seconds (default 60). That covers the forced drop, the sweep's leftovers query and drops, and the logins session.
  - A setting that is not a whole number from 1 to 3600 is refused before any connection: exit 2, "scenario-db: SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 3600, not '<value>'".
  - A drop that fails, forced or a sweep's, says "scenario-db: could not drop database <name>: <psql's last line>" (was the name alone), and the database is left for a later sweep.
  - The header says why.
- rsi/scenarios/237.sh (new), rsi/backlog/237.json.

What stays: every other scenario; the sweep's rules (no FORCE, nothing connected, older than SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_SWEEP_MINUTES); the logins rule; the 15433 refusal.

Files: rsi/scenarios/check-j02-lands.sh, scripts/blackbox/scenario-db.sh, rsi/scenarios/237.sh, rsi/backlog/237.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/237.sh, black box, on databases of its own on the test server:
- (1) check-j02-lands.sh runs whole with a `psql` first on PATH. At each "drop database" that psql counts the backends of the same run's other databases whose statement is a LISTEN, then runs the real psql. j02 exits 0; at least two drops are seen; every count is 0.
- (2) A listener on database a that reads nothing is flooded with notifications until its backend waits on ClientWrite (a harness fault if it never does within 10 batches of 2000). Then `scenario-db.sh drop b` with SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS=3, under a 20 s timeout:
  - it ends within 15 s;
  - it says "scenario-db: could not drop database <b>: ...";
  - b is still there.
  With the listener gone, the same drop removes b.
- (3) SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS soon, 0 (statement_timeout 0 is no bound) and 3601: each exit 2, the message names the setting, and nothing is dropped.
- (4) The sweep is bounded too: database c, a leftover under SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_SWEEP_MINUTES=0, and the listener of (2) stuck in ClientWrite again. `scenario-db.sh sweep <c>` with SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS=3, under a 20 s timeout, ends within 15 s, says "scenario-db: could not drop database <c>: ...", and c is still there. With the listener gone, the same sweep drops c.
- (5) The default bound is 60 s (the gate and the runners set no SPAWN_SCENARIO_DB_DROP_SECS): with the setting unset, `scenario-db.sh drop d` and `scenario-db.sh sweep d` run through a `psql` first on PATH that records each call's statements; every psql session they open sends "set statement_timeout = '60s'" before anything else, and d is dropped.
- (2) and (4) each hold the test server's drops for at most their 3 s bound (20 s on a candidate without one).
- On live main 9e1a8d22, 237.sh exits 1 at (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5).

Verified by: on the shared ccd cluster, no DROP ... WITH (FORCE) waits longer than 60 s from now on (pg_stat_activity), and a check-j02-lands.sh run leaves suite.lock within its normal minute.
